title: Does ML-NMR cost per effective draw grow with integration rows, or is sampler geometry what binds?
question: Decomposing multinma ML-NMR cost per effective draw into CPU per gradient (integration arithmetic) and gradients per effective draw (sampler geometry), does cost rise in proportion to integration points at realistic network sizes, and at what integration order does aggregate integration become the dominant part of each gradient?
design: CPU per gradient timed on multinma's compiled model over integration points, aggregate-study count, covariate dimension, binomial or M-spline survival outcome and fixed or random effects; gradients per effective draw counted from NUTS fits on a binomial and M-spline subgrid. 90 cells, 5 repeats each for timing cells and 3 for sampler cells.
